title: Check List & Test Report for Toilet Emergency Call
source: spec/Toilet_Emergency_Call_Test.html — the toilet emergency-call sibling of `fire-pwd-intercom-test.json`, and the same sheet down to the banner: a document block, the same three-item readiness checklist ticked YES / N/A / NO, a zone table whose headings each carry two bulleted sub-tests, and the same three-column sign-off. It differs only in what is tested per zone — Emergency Call Function and Siren / Lamp Function — and in the third readiness item's wording, which is carried verbatim from this file rather than from its sibling. The supplied file is a blank form (no record values to strip), and its six generic "Toilet E-call Zone n" headings are the form's own scaffolding, so they are seeded here; see the zone section note.

sections.title: Readiness Checks
sections._note:
`page_break_before` on the opening section is what keeps this on one sheet: `paginate` gives every section its own page unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op for layout — it is already page 1. Same idiom as `fire-pwd-intercom-test.json`.

The source's eight document fields are the record header rather than a section of their own: they are one grid on the paper, directly under the banner, and the header info block prints them the same way without spending a section heading on them. The paper seeds Drawing REV with "0"; that is a record value about a specific drawing, not a template default, so it is left blank.

The three readiness items are the paper's, verbatim — item 3 reads "Zone number labeling provided at control panel" here, shorter than the intercom sheet's wording, and is kept as written (matching the original wins, SPEC §5). `status` rather than `pass_fail_na` so the choices read YES / N/A / NO in the sheet's own order and wording; the outcomes make a "No" derivable as an outstanding item (SPEC §6). The paper has no remarks column against these items — the renderer always prints one, so it is labelled and left for whatever the engineer needs to qualify a N/A with.

sections.title: Zone Tests
sections._note:
**One row per zone, where the paper spends three.** The source writes a zone heading — "1. Toilet E-call Zone 1" — and hangs two bulleted sub-items beneath it, Emergency Call Function and Siren / Lamp Function, each with its own Passed / Failed / N/A dropdown. The two sub-items are the same for every zone, so they are columns, and a zone becomes a single row. That prints the same information in a third of the height and, more to the point, lets a block with twenty toilets be one record. Same shape as `fire-pwd-intercom-test.json`.

**The six zone names ARE seeded here, unlike the intercom sheet.** That template leaves them blank because its source was a filled record whose headings named real panels ("Fire Intercom Zone 67") — record data. This source is a blank form and its headings are generic scaffolding, so the six are carried as `prefilled_rows`; the engineer renames what the block actually has. They are seeded WITHOUT the source's "1." … "6." prefixes: `auto_number` already prints the serial, and carrying both would number every row twice — and would misnumber the moment a zone is deleted. `min_rows` is 1 rather than 6 so a two-toilet block can delete the spare rows; the seed decides what a blank record starts with, `min_rows` only sets the floor.

**Why this section starts page 2.** Measured on the live build for the identical intercom sheet: a page gives 877px to content, a zone row costs 35px, and the document block, readiness table, zone table and sign-off together overrun A4 even at the table's minimum. Breaking here gives page 1 to the document and readiness blocks and page 2 to the zones and sign-off, with room for about twelve zones before page 2 needs its own break.

This is also what replaces the source's "+ Add page" button: that clones the whole sheet, header and sign-off included, purely to get more zone rows. Here the table grows and the record stays one document with one sign-off.

sections.title: Sign-off
sections._note:
An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, which would add a third sheet carrying nothing but signatures. Both routes carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. Same idiom as `fire-pwd-intercom-test.json`.

The source's three columns, and it heads the lower two identically — "WITNESS BY" — so the roles read the same here; the distinct `stage` values are what drive the workflow (SPEC §6).

The paper's sign block carries only Name, Signature and Date — no company column. The renderer always prints Company, so Performed By defaults to Kenyon Pte Ltd and stays editable (unlocked, as on `staircase-pressurization.json`); the two witness companies are left blank for whoever attends.
